title: Why Your Blend Recommendation Comes From the Same Person Who Sells You the Blend
excerpt: Most co-op agronomists get their formulation guidance from manufacturer reps — the same reps whose compensation depends on which product gets recommended. That's not a knock on any individual rep; it's a structural problem.
author: Algaeo
content:
## The advice and the sale come from the same place

In most retail agronomy relationships, the person recommending a fertilizer blend and the person selling it are the same person, working for the same company, with compensation tied to volume moved. That doesn't make any individual rep dishonest — most are genuinely trying to help growers — but it does mean the recommendation isn't independent of the sale, structurally, no matter how good anyone's intentions are.

## What an independent tool actually changes

A formulation recommendation generated from a soil/crop/field-data model, with no product to sell attached to the output, removes that structural conflict entirely — not by asking anyone to be more virtuous, but by separating the two roles. The co-op agronomist still makes the final call; they just make it with a second, independent input instead of relying entirely on the manufacturer relationship.

## Where this fits into an existing workflow

This isn't a replacement for agronomist judgment or field experience — it's a second opinion, generated in seconds, that an agronomist can weigh against everything else they know about a specific field. The co-ops getting the most value from this treat it exactly that way: one more data point, not a black-box verdict.

title: What a Digital Twin Actually Does With Your Soil and Crop Data
excerpt: "Digital twin" gets thrown around loosely in ag-tech. Here's specifically what goes in, what happens to it, and what comes out, in plain language.
author: Algaeo
content:
## What goes in

Three categories of input drive a recommendation: soil type and test results (texture, organic matter, existing nutrient levels), crop type and target yield, and field-specific data where available (past application history, irrigation, regional climate norms). The model doesn't need all of it to produce a recommendation, but accuracy improves as more real field data is supplied instead of defaults.

## What happens in between

The model cross-references that input against a formulation logic built on established agronomic relationships — nutrient availability curves by soil type, crop-specific uptake patterns, and microbial dosing thresholds — rather than a single fixed recipe applied to every field. Two fields with the same crop but different soil texture and organic matter will get different recommendations, because they need different things.

## What comes out

A specific blend recommendation: ratios, application rate, timing, and microbial dosing guidance where relevant — something a co-op agronomist can act on directly, or adjust based on what they know about that specific grower's field that the model doesn't have. It's built to be a fast, independent second opinion, not a replacement for the agronomist making the final call.

title: Why Co-Ops Don't Need Us to Hold a Fertilizer Registration
excerpt: We get asked about this often enough that it's worth explaining directly: Algaeo doesn't manufacture, blend, or ship fertilizer, so state fertilizer registration isn't part of how this works.
author: Algaeo
content:
## What we actually sell

Algaeo is a subscription software product: a co-op agronomist enters soil type, crop type, and field data, and gets back a blend recommendation. We don't manufacture anything, we don't hold physical inventory, and no physical product ships from us to anyone.

## Why that matters for how you already operate

Your co-op already holds the fertilizer registration required to blend and distribute product in your state, the same way it does today. Nothing about that changes. What changes is where the formulation recommendation comes from — an independent model instead of (or alongside) a manufacturer rep — while your existing blending operation, registration, and distribution stay exactly as they are.

## The short version

We're a tool your agronomists use, not a product that enters your supply chain. That's a deliberate design choice, not an accident — it's what let us build something genuinely independent instead of another blend competing for shelf space.
